Definition: from G4328; apprehension (of evil); by implication, infliction anticipated:--expectation, looking after.
BiblicalUsage: Prosdokia means expectation, the looking forward to something dreaded or hoped for. Jesus says men's hearts will fail them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth, and Peter, freed from prison, says, Now I know of a surety that the Lord hath sent His angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe expectation cuts both ways: the world waits in fear for what is coming, and Peter waited in chains for what Herod planned, but God broke both expectations open.
